answer.rationale: Latency is climbing on the write path while settlement traffic peaks and writes are heavy. The release carries a required security patch and cannot be reverted, which rules out rollback_release. Capacity additions won't help under heavy write contention unless we cap the source of the slowdown. Memory b4 shows that circuit breakers on the payments dependency contained a partner-side issue by failing fast and preserving the rest of the checkout path. Here, the analogous move is to engage write-path protection — either a self-protection breaker on the slow write dependency or a circuit breaker around the downstream call that is most likely causing the latency inflation. This prevents write queue buildup and sheds load cleanly while keeping customer writes flowing where they can succeed. Read-replica routing (b5) does not address write-path latency. Regional failover (b2) is unwarranted unless region health is confirmed degraded — the current signal is write-path latency, not a regional incident. So the single intervention is enabling the circuit breaker to keep writes available and stop the latency cascade.
